note:
ISO 2026-W50 runs from December 7 through December 13. Mercury is about 1.6° in ecliptic longitude from Dschubba in Scorpius. To find Jupiter, first identify Leo, trace the Sickle, and locate Regulus in that pattern. Jupiter lies about 2.9° away in ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot; use the finder to transfer from Regulus to the planet.

**Naked eye:** 🌑 New Moon — 00:51:51 UTC. The dark Moon favors faint targets and extended star fields. Use Mothallah, Sheratan, Head of Hydrus, Almach, Hamal, β Tri as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -6.2; direct motion; 4.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Solar conjunction in ecliptic longitude Dec 09 00:51 UTC. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Dec 07 19:28 UTC. Conjunction with Pluto in ecliptic longitude Dec 12 23:53 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude -0.7; direct motion; 91.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Dec 07 19:28 UTC. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -4.8; direct motion; 32.6% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 0.4; direct motion; 90.2% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 7.5; retrograde motion; 98.6% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.2; direct motion; 99.2% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Station Dec 13 00:56 UTC: turns retrograde. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.6; retrograde motion; 99.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Station Dec 10 23:31 UTC: turns direct. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.6; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Station Dec 12 22:18 UTC: turns direct. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Dec 12 23:53 UTC.

**Binoculars:** Trace Pisces’s charted figure in the finder, then identify Alrescha at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** NGC 752: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Arp 78: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Double Cluster with 869: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Silver Needle: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

story_candidates.dek: Mothallah is a star in Tri of catalogue visual magnitude 3.42; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
The stored catalogue gives a visual magnitude of 3.42. This is a catalogue value, not a prediction of its brightness this week. Lower magnitudes mean brighter objects; sky brightness and altitude affect whether you can see the star.

Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 1h 53m and declination +29.6°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star rises and sets, reaching approximately 75° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Tri constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
